message: DROP CONSTRAINT DestinationCalendar_bookingId_fkey on DestinationCalendar removes a database-enforced invariant — application code that relies on it may break.
help: ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT removes whatever the constraint enforced: a FOREIGN KEY (referential integrity), CHECK (predicate validity), PRIMARY KEY (row uniqueness + non-null), or UNIQUE constraint. Application code that assumes the invariant holds will silently accept data that previously would have been rejected. Atlas free-tier breaks this into CD101 (FK), CD102 (CHECK), and CD103 (PK) because Atlas performs schema diffing and knows the constraint type. We cannot tell from `ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT name` alone — same warning regardless. Suppress with `-- safemigrate:ignore=constraint-dropped-warning reason="..."` after confirming the drop is intentional.

lock_impact.note: the real risk is losing the invariant, not the lock

message: ADD CONSTRAINT EventType_userId_fkey FOREIGN KEY on EventType without NOT VALID requires a full table scan.
help: Postgres validates the FOREIGN KEY against every existing row, holding SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE for the entire scan — that blocks writes on both the referencing and referenced table (reads still OK). On a large pre-existing table the scan runs for minutes. The two-step pattern is non-blocking: add the constraint with NOT VALID (catalog-only, ~millisecond lock), then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate migration which uses ShareUpdateExclusiveLock (doesn't block reads or writes).

lock_impact.blocks: writes on both the referencing and referenced table (reads still OK)
lock_impact.note: safe path: ADD ... NOT VALID (instant), then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (ShareUpdateExclusive — non-blocking)
